items.title: Section: Three Persons, Three Roots — Heedlessness, Indulgence, and Wrong Practice

items.zh: 復有三種補特伽羅，依三處引諸隨煩惱。云何三種補特伽羅？一、依正法而出家者，二、在居家受用欲者，三、正法外而出家者。云何三處引隨煩惱？所謂最初補特伽羅，依放逸處引隨煩惱。此復二種。謂或依內妄顯己德，為衣服等利養恭敬，自說己得勝過人法。或復依他諸有智者同梵行等，以身語業逼迫、加害、損惱、毀辱。當知第二補特伽羅，依耽欲處引隨煩惱。彼由耽著諸欲因緣，受用諸欲，依身語意行三惡行。當知第三補特伽羅，依邪行處引隨煩惱。略有三種，謂隨逐遠離、隨逐憒鬧、隨逐學處起隨煩惱。
items.en: There are also three kinds of person who, depending on three grounds, draw forth the secondary afflictions. What are the three kinds of person? One who has gone forth within the true Dharma; one who remains a householder enjoying desires; one who has gone forth outside the true Dharma. The first kind of person draws forth secondary afflictions depending on a ground of heedlessness: either falsely displaying one's own inner virtue for the sake of robes and other requisites, honour, and respect; or, depending on others, oppressing, harming, distressing, and humiliating the wise and one's fellow practitioners through bodily and verbal action. The second kind of person draws forth secondary afflictions depending on a ground of indulgence in desire: through the causes and conditions of indulging in desires, enjoying desires, one commits the three unwholesome conducts of body, speech, and mind. The third kind of person draws forth secondary afflictions depending on a ground of wrong practice, briefly of three kinds: secondary afflictions arising from pursuing solitude, pursuing rowdy company, and pursuing the training rules.

items.title: Section: The Non-Buddhist Ascetic Who Pursues Solitude in Vain

items.zh: 云何隨逐遠離起隨煩惱？謂諸外道隨逐遠離所有臥具，而為五蓋覆蔽其心。或住於苦，領受身心諸苦惱故。或復遠離煩惱對治，由離信等五種根故。彼由如是住染污故，住苦惱故，無有對治能除染污苦惱住故，是名隨逐遠離諸隨煩惱。
items.en: What are the secondary afflictions arising from pursuing solitude? Such non-Buddhist practitioners pursue remote dwellings and bedding, yet remain covered within by the five hindrances. Or they dwell in suffering, undergoing bodily and mental torment. Or they remain apart from the true antidote to affliction, having abandoned the five faculties beginning with faith. Because they dwell in defilement, dwell in suffering, and possess no antidote able to remove this defiled, suffering state, this is called the secondary afflictions arising from pursuing solitude.

items.zh: 云何隨逐憒鬧起隨煩惱？謂各別執異見、異欲相違言論，建立自品、他品差別，廣起忿、恨，乃至誑、諂。

items.title: Section: Wrong Practice Named in Full, and Wrong Training's Own Threefold Shape

items.zh: 是名隨逐憒鬧諸隨煩惱。云何隨逐學處起隨煩惱？謂觀自他現行諸罪，無有羞恥，毀戒、穿戒，是名隨逐增上戒學諸隨煩惱。若有依止世間等至，於其下劣計自為勝，或於相似計自為勝，心生高舉，是名隨逐增上心學諸隨煩惱。若少聽聞，不能觀察所有善法，是名隨逐增上慧學諸隨煩惱。如是一切，總略說名非法之行、不平等行。由非善義，名非法行；非愛果義，名不平等行。
items.en: This is called the secondary afflictions arising from pursuing rowdy company. What are the secondary afflictions arising from pursuing the training rules? Observing one's own or another's actual transgressions without shame, breaking the fundamental precepts or fraying the lesser ones, is called the secondary afflictions arising from pursuing the higher training in precepts. Relying on worldly attainment, and comparing oneself to those of lesser or equal attainment, giving rise to an inflated mind, is called the secondary afflictions arising from pursuing the higher training in mind. Having heard little and being unable to discern wholesome states, is called the secondary afflictions arising from pursuing the higher training in wisdom. All of this, in brief, is called non-dharma conduct and unequal conduct. Being contrary to what is wholesome is called non-dharma conduct; yielding an undesirable result is called unequal conduct.

items.title: Section: Ten Kasinas and the Miraculous Powers They Unlock

items.zh: 復次，若觀行者修十遍處，能為五事。何等為五？謂由修習地遍處等乃至白遍處故，便能引發化事、變事諸聖神通。又由修習空無邊處一切處故，便能引發往還無礙諸聖神通。
items.en: Furthermore, if a practitioner of the contemplative path cultivates the ten kasinas, this can accomplish five things. What are the five? By cultivating the earth kasina and so on through the white kasina, one draws forth the noble miraculous powers of creation and transformation. By cultivating the kasina of boundless space in all its pervasiveness, one draws forth the noble miraculous power of coming and going without hindrance.

items.title: Section: From Consciousness Without Bound to Cessation Itself

items.zh: 又由修習識無邊處一切處故，便能引發無諍、願智、無礙解等諸勝功德。又即由此識無邊處遍處成滿，便能成辦無所有處解脫，及非想非非想處解脫。又即由此成滿因故，便能證入想受滅解脫，最勝住所攝。又由識無邊處故，無邊無量遍滿行轉，是故此上不立遍處。
items.en: By cultivating the kasina of boundless consciousness in all its pervasiveness, one draws forth the excellent qualities of the absorption free of contention, aspirational wisdom, and the unhindered understandings. By this same completed and perfected kasina of boundless consciousness, one accomplishes the liberation of the base of nothingness and the liberation of the base of neither perception nor non-perception. By this same completing cause, one is able to enter the liberation of the cessation of feeling and perception, included among the most supreme of abidings. Because the base of boundless consciousness functions without boundary or measure, pervading all, no kasina is established beyond this point.

items.title: Section: How the Eight Liberations Are Purified — Clay, Kiln, and Wheel

items.zh: 勝處、遍處是諸解脫能清淨道。
items.en: The mastery-bases and the kasinas are the path able to purify the liberations.

items.title: Section: Liberation from the Cognitive Obstruction, and Three Ways Craving Clings to Absorption

items.zh: 又諸解脫，由所知障解脫所顯。由此聲聞及獨覺等，於所知障心得解脫。復次，略由三相，修等至者愛味等至。謂或證得等至，出已計為清淨，可欣、可樂、可愛、可意，隨念愛味。或未證得，或已證得，未來愛味增上力故，追求欣樂而生愛味。或已證得，計為清淨，可欣、可樂，乃至廣說現行愛味。若從定出可生愛味，若正在定無有愛味。言愛味者，謂於是中遍生貪著。
items.en: These liberations are manifested through liberation from the cognitive obstruction. Through this, śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas attain freedom of mind from the cognitive obstruction. There are, briefly, three characteristics by which one who cultivates meditative attainment comes to crave that attainment. Having attained it and emerged, holding it to be pure, delightful, lovely, and pleasing, and craving it through recollection. Whether not yet attained or already attained, through the enhancing power of craving for the future, pursuing and delighting in it. Or having attained it, holding it to be pure and delightful, and so on, giving rise to present, manifest craving. Craving can arise upon emerging from absorption; while actually within it, there is no craving. Craving means giving rise to pervasive attachment towards these states.

items.title: Section: Why a Higher Realm's Attainments Do Not Follow One Downwards Uninvited

items.zh: 復次，下地諸法若生上地，不現在前。上地諸法若生下地，其離欲者或現在前。若生下地，於上起愛，未得離欲不定心者，當言此愛是欲界繫。當知此愛或是染污、或不染
items.en: States belonging to a lower realm, if one is reborn into a higher realm, do not manifest. States belonging to a higher realm, if one is reborn into a lower realm, may manifest for one who has become free of desire. If one is reborn into a lower realm and craving arises towards a higher realm, for one who has not become free of desire and remains of unsettled mind, this craving should be said to be bound to the desire realm. One should know that this craving is either tainted or untainted.

items.zh: 污。云何染污？若生是心：我今云何當證如是廣大喜樂所隨等至。若得證者，我當如是如是愛味。又我云何當得生上，常恒不變。

blocks.text: How practice goes wrong, how the kasinas and the eight liberations work, and how even meditation can become an object of craving.

Master Cháng Bǎi: the third is an outside renunciant who, through wrong view, falsely shows spiritual power and praises himself. (Untranslated, 0645b15: secondary afflictions that follow from crowds: different views and wishes, quarrels, factions, anger, resentment, deceit.)
Master Cháng Bǎi: though they practise in quiet places, the five hindrances cover their minds; they think enduring suffering ends suffering.
Master Cháng Bǎi: violating grave precepts is breaking; violating lesser ones, fraying.
Master Cháng Bǎi: "creation" makes material things exist from nothing; "transformation" changes what exists. The space kasina draws forth unhindered coming and going.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the mastery-bases and kasinas make the eight liberations purer, like clay, kiln, and wheel.

subs.head: A part of the cognitive obstruction

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi: the obstruction to meditation is counted as part of the cognitive obstruction, and the eight liberations free one from that part, without making one a buddha. Craving for absorption takes three forms: recollecting, pursuing, and present craving; not inside absorption itself.

Master Cháng Bǎi: a higher realm's afflictions do not appear in one not yet free of lower desire. (Untranslated, 0645c23: tainted aspiration: "How can I attain such vast joy? I will savour it, and be reborn above forever.")
Even meditation can become an object of craving. The treatise's warning is gentle: meditate to leave desire, not to collect pleasant states.

quiz.q: On which three grounds do the three persons draw forth secondary afflictions?
options: those in the Dharma on wrong practice, householders on heedlessness, outsiders on indulgence
all three on heedlessness
those gone forth in the Dharma on heedlessness, householders on indulgence, outsiders on wrong practice
all three on indulgence in desire
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the third person is an outside renunciant who, through the wrong wisdom of wrong view, acts in distorted ways and thus draws forth many secondary afflictions. The treatise's order is heedlessness, indulgence, wrong practice.

quiz.q: This is rendered "falsely displaying one's own inner virtue for the sake of robes ..." What is the problem?
options: it omits the final boast of surpassing others, and 依內 means relying on oneself, paired with 依他
none: the last clause only repeats, and 依內 means inner virtue, as the lecture says
it omits 利養, gain
恭敬 should be deleted
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: relying on oneself, one falsely shows spiritual power; one praises oneself as surpassing others, hinting at having attained meditation or the path. The English loses this claim and turns the self-based 依內 into "inner virtue."

quiz.q: Why do outsiders pursuing solitude still have secondary afflictions, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: their dwellings are too near villages, and a truly remote place would end the problem
because they have not taken the five precepts
though in quiet places, their minds stay covered by the five hindrances, and their austerity leaves affliction uncut
because they do not believe in the gods
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: though they practise in quiet places, the five hindrances still cover their minds; they think enduring suffering ends suffering, not knowing that afflictions must be cut. Physical solitude alone removes nothing.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish breaking the precepts from fraying them?
options: breaking is by lay people, fraying by monastics, whose many rules have more holes
breaking is deliberate, fraying unintended
violating the grave upper-grade precepts is breaking; violating the lesser ones is fraying
breaking is bodily, fraying is verbal
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: violating the grave upper-grade precepts is the fault of breaking, and violating lesser ones the fault of fraying. The English "fundamental" and "lesser" fit this. Both belong to the secondary afflictions pursuing the higher precepts.

quiz.q: What does cultivating the earth kasina through the white kasina draw forth?
options: the noble power of coming and going without hindrance, since material elements can be passed through
the noble miraculous powers of creation and transformation
freedom from contention, aspirational wisdom, and unhindered understanding
the liberation of the cessation of feeling and perception
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: creation makes material things exist from nothing, and transformation changes what exists. Because the first eight kasinas give mastery over objects of form, they draw forth these two. Coming and going belongs to the space kasina.

quiz.q: Why does the kasina of boundless space draw forth coming and going without hindrance?
options: because it means meditating on all things as empty, and emptiness has no barrier anywhere
because on attaining the sphere of boundless space there is no obstruction by form
because the divine eye sees far
because the gods protect one
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: because in attaining the sphere of boundless space there is no obstruction by form, it can draw forth unhindered coming and going. The space kasina is the sphere of boundless space, not the emptiness of all things.

quiz.q: 無礙解 is rendered "unhindered eloquence." Compared with the lecture, why is this too narrow?
options: not narrow: 無礙解 is simply good speaking, and the lecture gives no other division, so it is complete
it should be "unhindered powers"
it should be merged with 願智
無礙解 has four kinds, of teachings, meanings, words, and eloquence, and this covers one
quiz.why: The lecture speaks of the four unhindered understandings, while "eloquence" is the name of only one. Master Cháng Bǎi explains that these qualities are qualities of mind, so mastery over the sphere of consciousness brings them.

quiz.q: Why is no kasina established beyond boundless consciousness?
options: because the two higher spheres are defiled and sages avoid them
because the two higher spheres offer no liberation
boundless contemplation culminates here, and the two higher spheres are not apart from consciousness
because only buddhas can enter them
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: nothingness and neither perception nor non-perception are also not apart from consciousness; boundless contemplation is complete here. The treatise says this sphere functions without bound, pervading all, so no further kasina is needed.

quiz.q: Through liberation from what are these liberations manifested?
options: the cognitive obstruction
the afflictive obstruction, since liberation means cutting afflictions
the obstruction of karma
the obstruction of ripened results
quiz.why: This may surprise readers. Master Cháng Bǎi: the obstruction to meditation is counted as a part of the cognitive obstruction, and the eight liberations free one from it, drawing forth noble powers and other qualities. It is a partial freedom.

quiz.q: Do śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas become buddhas by this freedom from the cognitive obstruction?
options: yes; once it is gone they equal the Buddha, as both the text and the lecture hold
no; the obstruction to meditation is only one kind, the cognitive obstruction being very broad
yes, but only pratyekabuddhas
yes, but only those liberated through wisdom
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this does not mean they become buddhas; the cognitive obstruction is wide, covering all ignorance clinging to phenomena, and the obstruction to meditation is one kind. The two vehicles cut part of it and do not gain the name of having severed it.

quiz.q: Which of these is not among the three characteristics of craving absorption?
options: craving it through recollection after emerging
craving arising while one is actually within it
pursuing and delighting in it through craving for the future
giving rise to present, manifest craving, once attained
quiz.why: The three are recollecting, pursuing, and present craving. The treatise excludes craving inside absorption. Master Cháng Bǎi: while actually in absorption one does not think how fine it is, and no craving arises. Craving comes on emerging.

quiz.q: What happens with states of one realm when one is born in the other?
options: born higher, lower states do not manifest; born lower, higher states may manifest for one free of desire
born higher, lower states keep manifesting; born lower, higher states never do
states of both realms may manifest freely
states of neither realm ever manifest
quiz.why: The treatise gives two rules. Master Cháng Bǎi: "may" excludes one not free of desire, for whom higher afflictions do not manifest. He notes that the first rule speaks of the general case, so it should not be pressed as allowing no exception.
